review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the repo for uses of the equivalence lemmas and `seqTendstoAeSeq_succ`. The file has no `@[simp]` lemmas and no custom simp sets, so I found no competing rules, bad orientation or loop risk. The `tendstoInMeasure_iff_*` lemmas are alternative characterizations of one predicate. They would not make good simp lemmas, because they have overlapping, non-canonical right-hand sides. Callers in ConvergenceInDistribution.lean already use them explicitly in `simp only` and `simpa [...]`. `seqTendstoAeSeq_succ` is the `n+1` equation of a structurally recursive definition. It is used only through `rw` in one place, and making it simp would only matter if the definition were unfolded, which downstream code does not do. I could not run Lean, so nothing about simp behavior was tested.
